# A looped `#id` read whole is answered on a compiled target only as a count of
# a loop that renders its copies wherever its component renders it
# (test_reach_looped_id_whole_runs.txt). One a condition decides, and a whole
# read that is no count, are refused where the test reads them, rather than
# left for the target's compiler to stop on. The interpreter answers both,
# being the reference.

! sngl test --platform=html guarded.sngl
stderr 'guarded.sngl:18:15: `title` names a copy per iteration, which a test reads one at a time, `title\[i\]`, or counts with `.length\(\)` where the loop renders its copies wherever the component renders it'

! sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go walked.sngl
stderr 'walked.sngl:15:18: `title` names a copy per iteration'

sngl test --platform=none guarded.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=none walked.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

-- guarded.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component card ui.node {
    var names = ["a", "b"]
    var shown = true
    ui.vbox {
        if shown {
            for var n = names {
                ui.text #title(value=n)
            }
        }
    }
}

func testGuarded(t test.Test, c card) {
    c.shown = false
    t.assert(c.title.length() == 0)
}

ui.window {
    card
}
-- walked.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component card ui.node {
    var names = ["a", "b"]
    ui.vbox {
        for var n = names {
            ui.text #title(value=n)
        }
    }
}

func testWalked(t test.Test, c card) {
    var seen = 0
    for var x = c.title {
        seen = seen + 1
    }
    t.assert(seen == 2)
}

ui.window {
    card
}
